symptom: A synthetic re-digested evidence map could include an extra reason key with count 0 and a matching taxonomy key with count 0 while preserving all aggregate counts. The runtime and JSON Schema allowed non-negative values, although the builder emits keys only after observing at least one reason or conflict. No actual database, K archive, odds, or production records were used.
lesson: An aggregate count sum and exact taxonomy match do not imply that each serialized reason/taxonomy key represents an observed event: matching zero-valued phantom keys can be added without changing any total or the content digest's semantic checks.
guardrail: Require strictly positive safe-integer values for every own reason-count and taxonomy-count entry in both runtime admission and JSON Schema. Preserve empty maps for zero observations and multi-reason row coverage; reject re-digested zero-valued keys while retaining valid evidence digest compatibility.
